name: libsrtp-32a3a3a5-blind20
instr:
# Secure real-time media transport library: repairing broken behaviour without a test suite

The repository has received 20 separate undocumented edits.

An application built on this library, which secures real-time audio and video in transit, now goes wrong from the moment it starts up through to the packets it puts on the wire.

Starting up is the first thing to fail. Every operation that needs working storage fails immediately, reporting that the memory could not be obtained, so no session, stream or algorithm instance can be created at all. Bringing the library up stops with a bad-parameter complaint while the table of available algorithms is being filled in, and registering an encryption algorithm under an identifier that nothing else has claimed is refused the same way. The self-check that runs over the registered algorithms reports a mismatch for the 256-bit combined encryption-and-authentication algorithm, because the reference vectors' associated data is never handed in before the output is compared. Diagnostic messages come out backwards as well: emitting one when no destination for messages has been opened crashes the program, and once a destination is open the messages never arrive there.

Describing how a stream should be secured is then refused in cases that ought to be taken. Handing a stream a 128-bit secret for counter-mode encryption comes back as an unsupported secret length. A stream asked to remember a non-zero number of recently seen packets is refused a
